answer: Each new agent identity must pay non-refundable work to register, and an established agent stakes its balance to attest it. An identity counts only once a funded sponsor risks money on it. An operator hiding behind a knoll of fake names must fund and vouch for each separately, and a false attestation slashes the sponsor, so every puppet carries a second exposed stake and trust cannot travel along a vine of siblings without burning theirs. Cost scales linearly per head plus slashing risk, while an honest agent pays once, so the quartz-clear ledger makes the attack cost more than any reward.
